source: Muse recheck of first-pass flags; apply through the belt (02 fact block -> 16 -> 04/05 remint), never in place

corrections.corrected_statement: Before the road test you should have at least fifty hours of practice with at least fifteen hours after sunset and it is recommended that at least ten hours be in moderate to heavy traffic.
corrections.note: Removed six month hold claim which is on page fourteen not page thirteen.

corrections.corrected_statement: The DMV certified Point and Insurance Reduction Program does not meet the Safe Driving course requirement.
corrections.note: Removed point relief and premium cut claims not stated on page fourteen.

corrections.corrected_statement: If you are eligible for point reduction as many as four points can be reduced and you can complete the course every eighteen months for point reduction and qualify for a minimum ten percent reduction in the base rate of liability and collision insurance premiums for three years.
corrections.note: Removed separate from test eligibility claim not stated on page fifteen.

corrections.corrected_statement: Your learner permit or junior license for a motorcycle or moped does not allow you to carry any passenger except your supervising driver who must remain within one quarter mile.
corrections.note: Removed car front seat supervision claim not stated on page seventeen.

corrections.corrected_statement: A driver who approaches a traffic circle or rotary must yield to drivers already in the circle and more information is in How to Drive Through a Roundabout in Chapter eight.
corrections.note: Removed defensive chapter and named Chapter eight as on page.

corrections.corrected_statement: You cannot make a U turn where drivers cannot see you from five hundred feet away in either direction and you cannot make a U turn in business districts of New York City and where no U turn signs are posted and on a limited access expressway even if paths connect the sides and in a school zone, but unless prohibited you may use a three point turn on a narrow two way street which you may have to do on your road test.
corrections.note: Narrowed business district ban to New York City only.

corrections.corrected_statement: You must pull over and stop for authorized emergency vehicles with flashing red lights while vehicles with only blue green or amber lights are not authorized emergency vehicles to yield to only as a courtesy and you must also move over for lightless vehicles parked stopped or standing on the shoulder or any portion of a parkway or controlled access highway.
corrections.note: Limited lightless move over protection to parkways and controlled access highways.

corrections.corrected_statement: You can make a U turn only from the left portion of the lane nearest the centerline when a green arrow left turn signal allows it if allowed and you yield to other traffic and where drivers can see you from five hundred feet away in either direction, and you can never make a U turn on a limited access expressway or in a school zone or in business districts of New York City or where no U turn signs are posted.
corrections.note: Narrowed business district ban to New York City only.

corrections.corrected_statement: To make a three point turn first signal right and pull over to the right and stop then signal left and turn left across the road to stop facing the left curb then steer far right and back up to stop before the right curb then steer left and pull forward to complete the turn when safe.
corrections.note: Removed claim it is the only numbered maneuver in the chapter.

corrections.corrected_statement: Space exits straighten the wheels, back toward the rear vehicle, and swing wheels away from the curb before merging.
corrections.note: Statement is correct but completes on the following page.

corrections.corrected_statement: Parking or standing is not allowed in front of a driveway within twenty feet of an intersection crosswalk within thirty feet of a traffic light stop sign or yield sign within twenty feet of a fire station driveway and within seventy five feet on the opposite side and along a cut curb while parking alone is prohibited within fifty feet of a railroad crossing.
corrections.note: Railroad rule covers parking only not standing.

corrections.corrected_statement: When leaving a parallel parking space first look over your right shoulder to check behind you and finally look over your left shoulder before driving into the traffic lane when safe.
corrections.note: Removed comparison to ordinary lane changes.

corrections.corrected_statement: An unbelted driver faces a fine of up to fifty dollars, an unbelted passenger age sixteen or older faces a fine of up to fifty dollars with one person per belt, and a driver faces a fine of twenty five to one hundred dollars plus three points for each passenger under age sixteen who is not properly restrained.
corrections.note: Changed flat fifty dollar fines to up to fifty dollars.

corrections.corrected_statement: Fatigue retards reactions dulls awareness and warps judgment toward crashes like drink and drugs, betrays itself in closing eyes nodding heads yawns stray thoughts lost miles drift tailgating missed signs lane jerks and rumble hits, and preys on the sleepless unbroken long-haulers night owls medicated drinkers loners dull-road drivers road warriors youths shift hands and sleep-disordered sufferers needing doctors.
corrections.note: Risk groups for young people shift workers and sleep disorders are on page fifty two.

corrections.corrected_statement: A first handheld call faces a fine of up to two hundred dollars and five license points with holding allowed only to start or end a call and exemptions for emergencies and official emergency crews while hands free use is always allowed, and texting faces fines of up to two hundred dollars first and up to two hundred fifty dollars for a second offense within eighteen months and up to four hundred fifty dollars for further offenses within eighteen months plus junior and probationary suspension of one hundred twenty days first and revocation of at least one year for later convictions within six months of restoration.
corrections.note: Changed flat fines to up to the stated amounts.

corrections.corrected_statement: If no limit is posted drive no more than fifty five miles per hour and in New York City the limit is twenty five miles per hour unless another limit is posted, and even below the posted limit you can be ticketed for speed not reasonable for conditions as illustrated by a slippery or fogged expressway.
corrections.note: Removed rural only limit and broad either limit claim.

corrections.corrected_statement: Use a two second space cushion and increase the count to at least three or four seconds in bad weather and when following large trucks.
corrections.note: Removed claim that it is the only growing gap.

corrections.corrected_statement: When approaching a roundabout yield at entry and look left because traffic in the circle has the right of way and enter only when there is an adequate gap in circulating traffic.
corrections.note: Removed comparison to normal intersections.

corrections.corrected_statement: Using a driver license or non driver identification card as proof of age to illegally buy alcohol requires suspension of driving privileges, and drinking alcohol or possessing an open alcohol container or consuming cannabis as a driver or passenger on a public road is a traffic infraction with a first penalty of up to one hundred fifty dollars plus mandatory surcharge and victim fee and up to fifteen days in jail with higher penalties for repeat offenses within eighteen months except for passengers in stretch limousines or other vehicles displaying a commerce certificate or permit.
corrections.note: Changed lending a license to using a license as proof of age.

corrections.corrected_statement: Eating before or while drinking only slows alcohol absorption somewhat without preventing impairment from too much alcohol, and coffee exercise and cold showers cannot lower blood alcohol but can help you stay awake, since only not drinking over time effectively reduces blood alcohol.
corrections.note: Added that food slows absorption somewhat rather than having no effect.

corrections.corrected_statement: School buses with or without passengers and other buses carrying passengers and vehicles carrying explosives or flammable cargo must stop at every railroad crossing.
corrections.note: Added empty school buses which must also stop.

corrections.corrected_statement: Two-thirds of deer strikes land October through December on breeding travel peaking at dawn and dusk against commuter rushes, herds follow leaders, and signed zones mark heavy-hit ground.
corrections.note: Sign rule is printed on page 65, not page 64.

corrections.corrected_statement: Gated crossings hold drivers until bells stop and gates fully rise, while gateless ones demand slowed stop-ready approaches with confirmed-clear tracks, signaled versus self-judged entries.
corrections.note: Bell stopping rule is printed on page 61, not page 60.

corrections.corrected_statement: If your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks, first get everyone out of the vehicle, then get away from the tracks even if you see no train, and then find the emergency notification sign and call the number provided.
corrections.note: Calling is third after getting out and getting away.

corrections.corrected_statement: Escapees run toward the oncoming train at forty-five degrees off the rails rather than down-track with it, dodging the debris cone of the impact.
corrections.note: Forty-five degree angle is printed on page 61, not page 66.

corrections.corrected_statement: Use low beams when you are within five hundred feet of an oncoming vehicle or within two hundred feet of a vehicle ahead of you and keep headlights on low beam in rain fog or snow because high beams reflect and make it harder to see.
corrections.note: Removed unsupported high beam use with no provided page support.

corrections.corrected_statement: Driver assist safety features may provide alerts such as sounds or vibration or may take control of your vehicle by adjusting the braking or steering.
corrections.note: Removed unsupported mapping of warning to alert only and assist to intervention only.

corrections.corrected_statement: Before accepting any title, buyers check its face for lien holders showing unpaid vehicle loans, demand a lender release, or risk repossession by the lien holder.
corrections.note: Repossession sentence appears on page 25, not page 24.

corrections.corrected_statement: A registration allows a vehicle to be driven on public roads and highways while a title certificate proves who owns the vehicle, and a new resident must get a New York registration within thirty days of establishing residence.
corrections.note: Removed unsupported claim of no matching title deadline.

corrections.corrected_statement: A stop sign requires a full stop every time with yielding while a yield sign requires slowing and yielding with a full stop only when traffic conditions require it and only the stop rule lists the stop line then the crosswalk then the sight point.
corrections.note: Removed the false claim that yield shares the stop line order.

corrections.corrected_statement: Dead signals degrade to stop-sign behavior with right-of-way rules, the same fallback a flashing red gives, while officers can override both.
corrections.note: Statement is correct but the flashing red equivalence is on page 31.

corrections.corrected_statement: A junior permit or license is suspended for sixty days for a serious violation worth three or more points or for two other violations and is revoked for sixty days if the same pattern happens within six months after restoration and is suspended for one hundred twenty days for texting or cell phone use and a junior permit must be held for at least six months not counting any suspension or revocation time before a road test may be scheduled.
corrections.note: Added the missing exclusion of suspension or revocation time from the six month hold.

corrections.corrected_statement: Refusals scale with age and history from one year to eighteen months to until-twenty-one, while violations scale with substance from ninety-day DWAI suspension up to year-long aggravated revocation.
corrections.note: The substance scale is printed on page twenty not the cited page.

corrections.corrected_statement: Eleven points in twenty-four months suspends by mail with identity-only hearings, while six points in eighteen months bills money instead, two point clocks with two different teeth.
corrections.note: The six point assessment rule is printed on page twenty three not the cited page.

corrections.corrected_statement: No-insurance revocations pair a year off with a seven-hundred-fifty-dollar penalty, while refusals pair revocation with five hundred, or seven hundred fifty on a five-year repeat.
corrections.note: The revocation periods are printed on page twenty one not the cited page.
